headline: Approved previous meeting minutes; team reviewed emergency activations, CERT team transition, and cooling center preparedness.
summary: The Emergency Management team reviewed last month's activity, including a hotel placement for a resident who lost power and cooling centers opened at the Senior Center and Police Station. The team discussed the EMPG grant, DPW coordination, school safety reviews, communication with MEMA and regional partners, upcoming training, and summer heat and cooling center plans, including donated water from Stop & Shop.

decision_evidence.quote: A motion was made and seconded to approve the previous meeting minutes. Motion carried.

plain_text:
Minutes
Room 108: Malden City Hall, 215 Pleasant St. Malden, MA,
Thursday July 24rd at 4PM
Meeting Began at 4PM
Approval of Previous Meeting Minutes
The minutes from the previous meetings were reviewed.
June meeting minutes remain available online. 
No corrections or issues were raised. 
A motion was made and seconded to approve the previous meeting minutes. 
Motion carried.
Previous Month - Emergency Activations
The team reviewed emergency activity from the previous month.
No formal Emergency Management activations occurred. 
One incident involved assisting a resident who had lost electrical service by arranging
temporary placement at a hotel. 
Cooling Center were activated at the Senior Center and Police Station
Upcoming Schedule / Activations
No upcoming Emergency Management activations or scheduled events requiring team action
were identified at this time.
CERT Team Update
Laura in Health and Human Service will be taking over CERT Team
There are no new updates at this time. 
Additional information is expected to be available at the next meeting. 
7. Emergency Management Performance Grant (EMPG)
The team discussed the status of the Emergency Management Performance Grant.
Required materials have been submitted. 
Department / Facility Updates
Public Facilities / DPW
The team discussed the need to connect with DPW regarding Emergency Management
meetings and participation. 
Elaina confirmed that DPW is budgeted for Emergency Management
JP Kelley will reach out to Paul Myers the new DPW director
The team also discussed keeping emergency signage/message boards throughout the City
updated as needed. 
Schools and Other Facilities
Schools and other municipal facilities are undergoing reviews focused on fire safety and
security. 
The team discussed reviewing evacuation plans and ensuring plans are consistent across City
facilities. 
Schools have emergency notification systems in place that require recipients to acknowledge
alerts. 
Recent drills have focused primarily on preparedness, verifying information, ensuring
accessibility, and confirming that staff are able to respond to notifications promptly. 
Emergency Communications / Special Events
The team discussed communications and preparedness surrounding recent large-scale events
and activities.
Communications and notifications have been distributed through existing channels to keep
relevant personnel informed. 
The team discussed coordination with MEMA and regional partners. 
MEMA representatives indicated that Malden's emergency management structure and regional
coordination have been viewed positively. 
No significant issues were reported during the recent events discussed. 
The team agreed that the City's planning and preparation efforts have been effective. 
Emergency Management Team Structure
The team discussed proposed changes to the Emergency Management structure following City
Council budget discussions.
The team also discussed the importance of maintaining communication between members,
particularly during an activation. 
The group noted that the City's text-message communication system has significantly improved
coordination and situational awareness among team members. 
Members emphasized the importance of receiving timely information so that all representatives
can respond accurately to questions and incidents within their respective departments. 
The team will continue discussing how to maintain strong communication and coordination as
the structure changes. 
Regional Coordination
The team discussed continued coordination with MEMA and the Mystic Regional Planning
Committee.
Regional partnerships were identified as an important resource for emergency planning and
response. 
Members noted the value of sharing information, resources, and best practices with
neighboring communities and regional emergency management partners. 
The team intends to maintain these relationships moving forward. 
1 Upcoming Training / Events
The team discussed an upcoming event/training opportunity and whether a representative
should attend.
Members will review the information and coordinate attendance as appropriate. 
Team members noted that attending these events provides an opportunity to maintain
relationships and stay informed about regional emergency management activities. 
Heat / Cooling Center Preparedness
The team discussed preparedness for summer heat and potential cooling center needs.
Recent temperatures have approached approximately 90 degrees, and cooling center have
been opened
Emergency Management will coordinate with Stop & Shop regarding donated bottled water. 
Donated water is stored at the Police Department and distributed for emergency situations and
community events as needed. 
Water may also be staged at locations such as the Community Center and Senior Center
during periods of extreme heat. 
The Police Department remains available as an additional location during regular operating
hours. 
The team emphasized that these locations are intended to provide cooling and hydration
assistance rather than overnight accommodations. 
Additional water and cooling resources will be distributed as needed based on weather
conditions and community needs.
1Other Business
No additional business was raised.
Adjournment
A motion was made to adjourn the meeting. End at 4:37PM
